decisions.basis: Official JMAG-Designer pages describe only an 'intuitive interface' and never disclose the GUI framework, so there is no official evidence for any specific stack nor to overturn pass1; since 'unknown' is not a permitted enum value, pass1 is retained.

Official documentation presents JMAG-Designer as the integrated core environment of the JMAG product configuration but states no explicit UI pattern, giving no official basis to overturn pass1; 'unknown' is not a permitted enum value, so pass1 is retained.

Official JMAG multiphysics page states 'Multiple disciplines are closely integrated in JMAG' and documents magnetic-thermal 'strong coupling' within one solver, which directly supports single_kernel over file exchange.

Official JMAG-Express Online product page documents a browser-based JMAG product ('No installation required', usable on tablets/smartphones), overturning pass1=false; confidence medium because the cloud offering is a family member (JMAG-Express Online) rather than JMAG-Designer itself.
Official JMAG products page states 'Since being released in 1983', giving 2026-1983=43 years since first documented public release, exactly as pass2 computed.

Official Cadence/Hexagon documentation shows MSC Nastran is a text input-deck (Case Control/Bulk Data, DMAP) driven solver with no GUI framework of its own documented (the classic Motif GUI belonged to the separate Patran product), so no official evidence overturns pass1; 'unknown' is not a permitted enum value, so pass1 is retained.

The solver ships as a command-line engine plus separate job-monitor utility per the official Installation and Operations Guide, with no officially documented unified UI pattern, so pass1 cannot be overturned with official evidence; 'unknown' is not a permitted enum value, so pass1 is retained.
The official Cadence MSC Nastran product page lists 'Co-simulate across multiple disciplines' among its key benefits, which is direct vendor documentation of a co-simulation coupling strategy.
Official MSC Software blog states 'MSC released a commercial version of NASTRAN, MSC Nastran, in 1971', giving 2026-1971=55 years since first documented public release.

Official site defines PrePoMax as 'an open-source pre and post-processor for the Calculix FEM solver', i.e., a structural-FEA pre/post-processor rather than a generic open CAE platform, which clearly supports structure_fea.

Official site and full manual describe features and a .NET/Windows implementation but never characterize the overall software architecture, so there is no official evidence to overturn pass1; 'unknown' is not a permitted enum value, so pass1 is retained.
The official PrePoMax manual documents 'Advisor - opens an interactive helper that will guide the user through the main steps to set up' a model, directly verifying workflow_guide=true.
The official PrePoMax news archive records version 0.3.0 released 09/12/2016 as the earliest documented public release, giving 2026-2016=10 years.
